Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 43
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: In a relationship
  occupation: Chef
  trauma_type: Life-threatening illness
  pcl5: 80

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Emotional Numbing: I numb my feelings, Avoid Positive Events: Situations that might make me feel happy or hopeful, Delay Sleep: stay up until very late
  Threat: Flashbacks: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again, Body Reacts Before Mind: My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think, Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
  Memory: Full Sensory Reliving: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once, Story Feels Unreal: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me, Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
  Negative Appraisals: Lost Emotions: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again, Body as Enemy: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe, Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened

Vignette:
Giulia had always taken pride in her work as a chef, whipping up intricate sauces and precision-cut vegetables with ease. But that was before she spent 10 days in the ICU, her body ravaged by a life-threatening case of sepsis. The memories of those days were hazy, but certain moments remained etched in her mind: the sound of beeping machines, the feeling of tubes snaking into her veins, and the numbness that had spread through her body like ice. As she slowly recovered, Giulia began to notice that she was avoiding things that might bring her joy. She would turn down invitations from friends, claiming exhaustion, and skip family gatherings, citing a need for quiet time. It wasn't just social events; even simple pleasures like reading or watching movies seemed too taxing. She felt numb, as if her emotions had been put on ice alongside her body. At night, Giulia found herself lying awake until the early hours of the morning, replaying the memories of her hospitalization in vivid detail. The sounds, smells, and sensations came flooding back: the antiseptic tang of the hospital soap, the feel of the ventilator tube digging into her skin, and the crushing sense of helplessness that had gripped her as she lay unable to move or speak. When these flashbacks hit, Giulia's body would respond before her mind could catch up. Her heart would racing, her muscles tensing, and her breath catching in her throat. She felt like she was reliving those terrifying moments all over again, powerless to stop the memories from hijacking her senses. Even when she knew she was safe – lying in bed with her partner beside her – Giulia couldn't shake off the feeling of being on high alert. These episodes left her reeling, struggling to separate past and present. The memory of her ordeal felt both completely real and utterly unreal at the same time. When it came flooding back, Giulia was overwhelmed by grief, as if she was mourning the loss of some essential part of herself. Her body seemed to have developed a twisted relationship with danger, reacting as if she were still in peril even when there was no apparent threat. As a result, Giulia had come to believe that her emotions would never be the same again. She felt lost and disconnected from her own feelings, like she was observing her life from outside her body. Her body itself seemed treacherous, prone to wild swings of adrenaline and numbness. And deep down, she knew that it had been permanently damaged by what happened – a conviction that filled her with a creeping sense of vulnerability. These fears began to seep into her work as a chef. Simple tasks like chopping vegetables or stirring sauces became fraught with anxiety. She would tense up at the sound of sizzling meat or the sight of sharp knives, her body reacting before she could calm it down. Her partner and colleagues noticed the change in her, commenting on how distant and preoccupied she seemed. It was only when Giulia found herself struggling to keep up with the demands of her job – missing orders, botching recipes, and snapping at staff – that she realized she needed help. She couldn't shake off the feeling that she was losing control, that her body and mind were conspiring against her. With a growing sense of desperation, Giulia made an appointment to see a therapist, hoping to somehow quiet the memories that haunted her and rediscover the emotions she had lost.
